[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called nuclear fission reaction?","marks":1,"answer":"The splitting of heavy atomic nucleans, such that of uranium, plutonium, into two fragments of roughly equal mass is called nuclear fission reaction."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Edible salt is highly electrolyte matter–Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Chemical compound cannot conduct electricity in their solid phase. In this case, the positive and negative ions of that compound are located in a fixed place and shows reluctance towards conducting electricity. But at liquid phase or in aqueous phase, the ions can move freely. Thus, at this stage, ionic compound like NaCl or other ionic compounds can conduct electricity through exchanging ions in aqueous phase or in liquid phase.
\[
\text{NaCl} \rightarrow \text{Na}^+(t) + \text{Cl}^-(t) \text{[Liquefied phase]}
\]
\[
\text{NaCl(s)} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}(t)} \text{Na}^+(aq) + \text{Cl}^-(aq) \text{[Aqueous phase]}
\]"},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Describe the mechanism of producing electricity of the cell of stem.","marks":3,"answer":"The elements having 26 and 29 atomic number in the stem are Fe and Cu respectively.
The cell reaction is,
\[
\text{Fe(s)} + \text{CuSO}_4(aq) \rightarrow \text{FeSO}_4(aq) + \text{Cu(s)}
\]
or,
\[
\text{Fe(s)} + \text{Cu}^{2+}(aq) \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{2+}(aq) + \text{Cu(s)}
\]
Here, Electricity can be produced using the products and reactants of this reaction.
A Copper rod is dipped into copper sulfate solution in a beaker as cathode. This is represented by \(\text{Cu/Cu}^{2+}\) (aq) symbol.
On the other beaker an iron rod is placed in ferrous sulfate solution as anode. Which is represented as \(\text{Fe/Fe}^{2+}\)(aq).
If two electrodes \(\text{Fe/Fe}^{2+}\) and \(\text{Cu}^{2+}\)/\(\text{Cu}\) to are connected by conducting wire then Daniel cell is formed which produces electricity.
In daniel cell \(\text{Cu/Cu}^{2+}\) (aq) metal/metal ion electrode is used as cathode and \(\text{Fe/Fe}^{2+}\)(aq) metal/metal ion electrode is used as anode. To connect the two solutions of two jars, a U-shaped tube consisting neutral electrolyte (KCl) is dipped into both solution. Now, if the two electrodes are connected through a wire, then the following spontaneous oxidation-reduction reaction will occur.
\[
\text{Anode reaction: Fe(s)} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{2+}(aq) + 2e^-
\]
\[
\text{Cathode reaction: Cu}^{2+}(aq) + 2e^- \rightarrow \text{Cu(s)}
\]
\[
\text{Fe(s)} + \text{Cu}^{2+}(aq) \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{2+}(aq) + \text{Cu(s)}
\]
Which means, Fe atom of anode will convert itself into \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\) ion and mix with the solution. On the other hand, \(\text{Cu}^{2+}\) ion from the solution receives electron from cathode and preserve in the cathode converting itself into Cu atom. Actually, electrons flow anode to cathode for maintaining the electron balance and the flow of electron means current flow.
Hence, Electricity can be produced from daniel cell by indirectly connecting the two electrodes through salt bridge and wire."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Precipitation is produced by adding few drops of dilute NaOH in the aqueous salts of two containers of the stem–Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":"The salts of the two pots are of Fe and Cu. Precipitate will be produced after adding diluted NaOH solution on the aqueous solutions of those salts.
(i) Taking \(\text{FeSO}_4\) aqueous solution in a test tube and adding a few drops of NaOH, Ferrous hydroxide precipitate of green color is produced and \(\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4\) remains in the water as soluble mixture. The corresponding reaction:
\[
\text{FeSO}_4 + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Fe(OH)}_2\downarrow + \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4
\]
(ii) Now taking aqueous solution of \(\text{CuSO}_4\) into a test tube, a few drops of diluted NaOH solution is added to it. Then precipitation of copper Hydroxide [\(\text{Cu(OH)}_2\)] of light blue color is produced and \(\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4\) remains in the water as soluble mixture. Corresponding reaction is:
\[
\text{CuSO}_4 + 2\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Cu(OH)}_2\downarrow + \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4
\]
---"}]

subject: Chemistry
question:
\[
\text{AlCl}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{X} + \text{Y} (\text{Acidic}).
\]
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is symbol?","marks":1,"answer":"Symbol is an abbreviation for an element. The abbreviated form of English or Latin name of the element is used as a symbol of that element."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why are sewing needles kept in coconut oil?","marks":2,"answer":"Sewing needles iron can get decayed or eroded due to chemical reaction with oxygen and water vapor of air. If sewing needles are kept in coconut oil, oil will prevent it from coming in direct contact with oxygen and water vapor thus prevent from corrosion. That's why sewing needles are kept in coconut oil."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"What type of reaction in stem it is? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"\[
\text{AlCl}_3 (\text{s}) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} (\text{l}) \longrightarrow \text{Al(OH)}_3 (\text{s}) + 3\text{HCl} (\text{aq}) (\text{acidic})
\]
The chemical reactions, in which water as a reactant reacts with other compounds and produce some new compounds is called hydrolysis.
Here, \(\text{AlCl}_3\) and \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) are participating in a reaction so it is a hydrolysis reaction. This kind of reaction sometimes produces non-transparent soluble compounds. In that case, the reaction may be considered as a precipitation reaction. Here, \(\text{Al(OH)}_3\) is non-soluble in water So this reaction can be classified as both hydrolysis reaction and precipitation reaction."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"X and Y compounds are opposite properties—Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":"\[
\text{AlCl}_3 (\text{s}) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} (\text{l}) \longrightarrow \text{Al(OH)}_3 (\text{s}) + 3\text{HCl} (\text{aq}) (\text{acidic})
\]
So X is \(\text{Al(OH)}_3\) and Y is \(\text{HCl}\) (\(\text{acidic}\)).
Y is acidic because when dissolved in water it decomposes into hydrogen ion or proton (\(\text{H}^+\)) which is a characteristic of acid.
\[
\text{HCl} (\text{aq}) \longrightarrow \text{H}^+ (\text{aq}) + \text{Cl}^- (\text{aq})
\]
Moreover, acid undergoes reaction with metallic oxide and produces salt and water
\[
\text{CaO} (\text{metallic oxide}) + 2\text{HCl} = \text{CaCl}_2 (\text{salt}) + \text{H}_2\text{O}
\]
So HCl is acidic in nature.
On the other hand \(\text{Al(OH)}_3\) reacts with acid and produces salt and water
\[
\text{Al(OH)}_3 + 3\text{HCl} (\text{acid}) = \text{AlCl}_3 (\text{salt}) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} (\text{water})
\]
\(\text{Al(OH)}_3\) is basic in nature. So X (\(\text{Al(OH)}_3\)) and Y (\(\text{HCl}\)) components are opposite in nature.
---"}]

parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called coinage metal?","marks":1,"answer":"Group 11 (IB) metals are called coinage metals. Copper, silver, gold, and roentgenium."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why element Ne does not form any compound? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"The atomic number of neon is 10. Its electron configuration is—
\[
\text{nNe} \rightarrow 1s^2 [2s^2 2p^6]
\]
From the electron configuration, we see that there are 8 electrons in the last orbit of Ne. This is a really stable electronic structure for Ne. Ne doesn't lose, gain or share an electron with any other element due to this stable electronic structure. So, it doesn't form chemical bonds. Therefore, it doesn't react with anyone and presents an inert state."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Write down the identification reaction of the presence of \(\text{Y}^{2+}\) ion in any salt solution.","marks":3,"answer":"In the stem, Y is copper.
Identifying \(\text{Y}^{2+}\) or \(\text{Cu}^{2+}\) in any salt solution by using \(\text{NaOH(aq)}\):
Adding NaOH to the liquid solution of copper salts results in the blue precipitate of copper hydroxide.
\[
\text{CuCl}_2 (\text{aq}) + 2 \text{NaOH} (\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{Cu(OH)}_2 (\text{s}) + 2\text{NaCl} (\text{Light blue precipitate})
\]
This reaction is used to identify the presence of \(\text{Cu}^{2+}\) ion in any salt solution by its light blue precipitate."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the order of the size of the elements X, Y and Z.","marks":4,"answer":"According to the stem, the atomic number of elements X, Y and Z are 12, 29 and 18.
Their electronic configurations are:
\[
\text{X}(12): 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 [3s^2]
\]
\[
\text{Y}(29): 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 [4s^1 3d^{10}]
\]
\[
\text{Z}(18): 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 [3s^2 3p^6]
\]
So, their positions in periodic table are:
X: Period 3, Group 2
Y: Period 4, Group 11
Z: Period 3, Group 18
The atomic size of elements decreases from left to right in a period.
So, in terms of atomic size — X > Z.
Again, the atomic size of elements increases from top to bottom in a group.
So, in terms of atomic size — Y > X.
Therefore, Y > X > Z in terms of atomic size.
---"}]

In contact process, some \(\text{O}_2\) gas is passed with \(\text{SO}_2\) in a furnace. Write your opinion.","marks":4,"answer":"The compound Y of the stem produced in contact process is \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\). It is used as both oxidizing agent and dehydrating agent.
\(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) as an oxidising agent: Copper does not react with hydrochloric acid but reacts with concentrated sulphuric acid because of the oxidation properties of sulphuric acid. The acid produces atomic oxygen and reacts with metals in the following ways.
\[
\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{SO}_2 + [\text{O}] (\text{Concentrated})
\]
Produced atomic oxygen in the reaction oxidizes the metals which are less active than copper or hydrogen produce metal oxides. Metal oxides react with acids and produce acid and water. So, \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) shows the properties of an oxidizing agent.
\(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) as a dehydrating agent: When few drops of concentrated \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) are added to the sugar or sucrose (\(\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}\)), it produces steaming black carbon foam. The sulphuric acid dehydrates the carbohydrate sugar, removing the water and heating it into steam leaving behind the carbon foam:
\[
\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}(\text{sugar}) + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4(\text{sulphuric acid}) \rightarrow 12 \text{C} (\text{carbon}) + 11 \text{H}_2\text{O} (\text{water})
\]
This is how \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) acts as a dehydrating agent.
---"}]

lesson: Hardness of Water and Acid Rain
question: Different salts dissolve in the water from "Acid Rain" when it flows along the Earth surface and this creates water's special characteristics "Hardness of water".
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is pH?","marks":1,"answer":"pH is the concentration of hydrogen ion."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why doesn't soap produce foam in hard water?","marks":2,"answer":"Soap is a sodium or potassium salt of higher organic acid. On the other hand, calcium or magnesium chloride, sulfate, carbonate or bicarbonate etc. salts dissolved in the water creates hardness. Sodium or magnesium ion in soap produces soluble sodium or potassium salt by reacting with calcium or magnesium salt. But calcium or magnesium salt in hard water doesn't give similar reaction with soap rather it forms an insoluble precipitate. So, soap doesn't produce any foam in hard water."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain how the special characteristics of water mentioned in the stem forms using equations.","marks":3,"answer":"The special characteristics of water mentioned in the stem is hardness. The causes of hard water are discussed below with reactions:
We know, a certain part of water in the water cycle flows along the surface of Earth. While flowing, this water comes in contact with different mineral salts present in the soil. So, salts are dissolved in the water. Rainwater reacts with \(\text{CO}_2\) to form carbonic acid. This carbonic acid present in rain water slowly reacts while flowing over limestone \(\text{CaCO}_3\), dolomite \(\text{CaCO}_3\), \(\text{MgCO}_3\) etc. rocks and dissolve these salts.
\[
\text{H}_2\text{O(l)} + \text{CO}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{CO}_3(\text{aq})
\]
Carbonic Acid
\[
\text{CaCO}_3(\text{s}) + \text{H}_2\text{CO}_3(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2(\text{aq})
\]
\[
\text{MgCO}_3(\text{s}) + \text{H}_2\text{CO}_3(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{Mg(HCO}_3)_2(\text{aq})
\]
The presence of these elements or \(\text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2\) and \(\text{Mg(HCO}_3)_2\) causes hardness in water."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the causes and results of the rain mentioned in the stem.","marks":4,"answer":"The causes and results of acid rain is analyzed below:
Usually sulphur and nitrogen oxides (\(\text{SO}_x\) and \(\text{NO}_x\)) create acid rain.
Sulphur dioxide (\(\text{SO}_2\)) and nitrogen dioxide (\(\text{NO}_2\)) has a lot of effect on the environment. Lightning produces nitrogen dioxide in the atmosphere. The produced nitrogen dioxide reacts with water present in water and produces nitric and nitrous acid.
\[
2\text{NO}_2(\text{g}) + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{HNO}_2(\text{aq}) + \text{HNO}_3(\text{aq})
\]
Nitrous acid is a weak acid. Oxygen present in the air oxidizes it and forms nitric acid.
\[
\text{HNO}_2(l) + \text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{HNO}_3(l)
\]
Similarly, power plants, brick kilns, industries use coal and petroleum with sulfur which produces sulphur oxides in the atmosphere. This sulphur dioxide reacts with oxygen and ozone in the air and produces sulphur trioxide. Later, sulphur trioxide reacts with the water in air and again produces sulphuric acid.
\[
\text{SO}_2(\text{g}) + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_3(\text{aq})
\]
\[
\text{SO}_3(\text{g}) + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4(\text{aq})
\]
These acids come down with rainwater as acid rain on Earth. This acid rain drops pH value of water bodies and soil to 4 or even less than 4. So, soil and water become acidic. Acidic soil reduces soil fertility and crop production. On the other hand, acidic water bodies become uninhabitable for fishes and other water organisms. Acid rain harms buildings and other heritage sites, sculptures etc.
---"}]

Explain","marks":2,"answer":"The neutralization reaction between a strong acid and a strong base always involves the same fundamental process: H⁺ ions from the acid react with OH⁻ ions from the base to form water.
\[
\text{H}^+(\text{aq}) + \text{OH}^-(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \quad \Delta H = -57.3 \, \text{kJ/mol}
\]
Regardless of which strong acid or strong base is used, this ionic reaction is the same. Since the same chemical change occurs (formation of one mole of water from H⁺ and OH⁻ ions), the enthalpy change (ΔH) is always the same value of approximately -57.3 kJ/mol. This is why the heat of neutralization for strong acid-strong base reactions is constant."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"How much water is to mix in Pot-A to make it semi molar solution?","marks":3,"answer":"For pot A in the stem, to make a semi-molar solution—

For example: in \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\), the subscript 2 indicates that the water molecule contains two atoms of hydrogen and one atom of oxygen."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"If you heated water sample A what happen? Explain with reaction.","marks":3,"answer":"Aqueous sample solution A in the stem contains various ions such as \(\text{Ca}^{2+}, \text{Mg}^{2+}, \text{Fe}^{3+}\) and \(\text{HCO}_3^-\).
When bicarbonate (\(\text{HCO}_3^-\)) salts of calcium, magnesium, iron, etc. are dissolved in water, the hardness formed is called temporary hardness and this water is called temporary hard water. That is, the aqueous solution of A or water has temporary hardness. Heating temporary hard water produces insoluble carbonate salts. This salt gathers at the bottom of the container as a precipitate. By separating these salts it is possible to turn temporary hard water into soft water.
\[
\text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{CaCO}_3(\text{s}) + \text{CO}_2(\text{g}) + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)}
\]
\[
\text{Mg(HCO}_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{MgCO}_3(\text{s}) + \text{CO}_2(\text{g}) + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)}
\]
\[
2\text{Fe(HCO}_3)_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{Fe}_2(\text{CO}_3)_3 (\text{s}) + 3\text{CO}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O(l)}
\]"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"How can you purify stem water sample B? Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":"Aqueous solution B in the stem contains various ions such as \(\text{Ca}^{2+}, \text{Mg}^{2+}, \text{Fe}^{3+}, \text{Cl}^-\) and \(\text{SO}_4^{2-}\).
If chloride or sulfate salts of calcium, magnesium, iron, etc. are dissolved in any water, permanent hardness occurs and this water is called permanent hard water. That is, the aqueous solution of B or water has permanent hardness. Permanent hardness cannot be removed by heating water. Permanent hardness is removed through different reactions or by adopting different methods.
Permanent Hardness Removal or Purification Method: When sodium carbonate is added to permanent hard water, it reacts with calcium ions, magnesium ions, and iron ions to produce calcium carbonate, magnesium carbonate, and iron carbonate precipitation. As a result, calcium ions, magnesium ions, and iron ions are removed from the water, i.e. permanent hardness is removed.
\[
\text{CaCl}_2 + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow \text{CaCO}_3 + 2\text{NaCl}
\]
\[
\text{MgCl}_2 + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MgCO}_3 + 2\text{NaCl}
\]
\[
2\text{FeCl}_3 + 3\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow \text{Fe}_2(\text{CO}_3)_3 + 6\text{NaCl}
\]
\[
\text{CaSO}_4 + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow \text{CaCO}_3 + \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4
\]
\[
\text{MgSO}_4 + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MgCO}_3 + \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4
\]
\[
\text{Fe}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3 + 3\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow \text{Fe}_2(\text{CO}_3)_3 + 3\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4
\]
---"}]

\]
\[
\text{H}^+ + \text{Cl}^- + \text{Na}^+ + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{Na}^+ + \text{Cl}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O}
\]
From the above reaction, it is seen that there is no change in the oxidation number of hydrogen (H), chlorine (Cl), sodium (Na), and oxygen (O). That is, no transfer of electrons takes place in this reaction. Only ions are exchanged. Hence, the reduction reaction is a non-redox reaction."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Aqueous solution of Z gas is basic–Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"Completing the first reaction of the catalyst gives-
\[
\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(\text{g}) + \text{heat}
\]
So, Z is ammonia (\(\text{NH}_3\)).
Aqueous solution of \(\text{NH}_3\) is alkaline.
When ammonia is dissolved in water, ammonia gas reacts with water to form the ammonium hydroxide ion.
\[
\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{NH}_4\text{OH}
\]
\[
\text{NH}_4\text{OH} \rightleftharpoons \text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^-
\]
Compounds that give hydroxide ions in aqueous solution are bases. Since, an aqueous solution of ammonia contains hydroxide ions, aqueous solution of ammonia is alkaline (aqueous solution of ammonia contains a small number of ammonium ions and hydroxide ions. Hence ammonia is a weak base)."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Describe the effect of temperature, pressure on the equilibrium of first reaction according to Le-Chatelier’s principle.","marks":4,"answer":"By completing the reaction of the stem -
\[
\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(\text{g}) + \text{heat} (\text{kJ})
\]
The effect of temperature and pressure on the equilibrium of the reaction is explained below.
Effect of temperature: The value of \(\Delta H\) in this reaction is negative ie, the forward part of the reaction is exothermic and the reverse reaction is endothermic. Increasing the temperature at equilibrium for this reaction will shift the equilibrium to the left and increase the amount of reactants. That is, by increasing the exothermic reaction, the effects of heat increase will be mitigated. Similarly, lowering the temperature at equilibrium will shift the equilibrium to the right and reduce the effect of lowering the temperature. As a result, the amount of production will also increase.
Effect of Pressure: Pressure affects the equilibrium of gaseous reversible reactions. Total number of moles of reactants is 4 and the products are 2. That is, the volume of production is less. Here the number of molecules decreases if the reaction is forward. As a result the pressure also decreases in the same volume. In this case, an increase in pressure will shift the equilibrium to the right and increase the yield. On the other hand, lowering the pressure at equilibrium will shift the equilibrium to the left and increase the amount of reactants, mitigating the effect of lowering the pressure.

Adding Na₂CO₃: As acetic acid is stronger than carbonic acid, it will react with sodium carbonate to produce sodium acetate, carbon dioxide gas, and water.

\]
Mixing NaOH: NaOH is a strong alkali. It reacts rapidly with acetic acid to form sodium acetate (salt) and water.
\[
\text{NaOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COONa} + \text{H}_2\text{O}
\]"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"The reactions between A and B type substances occurred in gastric pain treatment and nursing of soil for cultivation - Analyze the matter.","marks":4,"answer":"Stimulus 'A' is acid and 'B' is base. The reaction of A and B is a neutralization reaction.
Neutralization reactions are very important in our daily lives. Neutralization reactions occur in both cultivation (soil care) and gastric acidity elimination.
Usually, antacids are taken for heartburn due to acidity. When excess HCl is secreted into the stomach, the pH of the stomach drops, causing abdominal pain. Antacids are usually Al(OH)₃ (marketed as Aludox) and Mg(OH)₂ (marketed as milk of magnesia). The reaction of HCl secreted in the stomach and antacids is the neutralization reaction. Because antacids are alkaline. The neutralization reactions are as follows -
\[
\text{Al(OH)}_3 + 3\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{AlCl}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}
\]
\[
\text{Mg(OH)}_2 + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{MgCl}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}
\]
Again, a deficit of nitrogen or nitrate salts in the soil or the soil becoming acidic requires urea. If the soil becomes slightly basic, it requires (NH₄)₂SO₄. Because, when urea is dissolved in the soil, it slowly separates into NH₃ and CO₂ under the influence of an enzyme called urease. NH₃ dissolves in water to form NH₄OH which is partially dissociated into NH₄⁺ and OH⁻ ions. Plants absorb NH₄⁺ ions.
\[
\text{NH}_2 - \text{CO} - \text{NH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Urease}} \text{NH}_3 + \text{CO}_2
\]
\[
\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{NH}_4\text{OH}
\]
\[
\text{NH}_4\text{OH} \rightleftharpoons \text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^-
\]
On the other hand, (NH₄)₂SO₄ is a granular material and has acidic behaviour in aqueous solution.
\[
(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_4\text{OH} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4
\]
Weak base + Strong acid
(NH₄)₂SO₄ is applied if the soil becomes alkaline. It lowers the alkalinity and controls the pH of the soil. When the pH of the soil decreases due to acid rain or other factors, lime (CaO or Ca(OH)₂) is added to neutralize the acidity and raise the pH to suitable levels for plant growth."}]
